decision_summary: The bounded static-batch managed Prefect support profile passed every AC058 gate, adjacent phase gate, and acceptance checkbox in #290–#298. The candidate is qualified for the support profile below; publication in a 0.58 release remains separate.

support_profile.etlantic_packages: 0.57.2 candidate wheels from the qualified phase-0.58 source commit

issue_acceptance_map.title: [Epic][etlantic-prefect] Add managed Prefect execution on ETLantic's durable runtime

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Existing local direct execution remains compatible with isolated correlation and tested failure/concurrency behavior.
Remote execution uses only trusted immutable accepted inputs and a public targeted execution path.
Dispatch response loss and duplicate delivery recover without bypassing ETLantic ownership or replaying uncertain effects.
Status/cancellation preserve distinct orchestration, execution, and effect/publication evidence.
Recurring triggers preserve canonical firing identity and fresh admission with one timer authority.
Installed-artifact, live-worker, PostgreSQL, trust/revocation, and crash tests establish the exact published matrix.
Runnable host examples reuse the existing API; qualification claims and skips are explicit.

issue_acceptance_map.title: [feature][etlantic-prefect] Isolate direct-run state and qualify scheduler failure semantics

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Barrier-controlled overlapping calls on the same scheduler instance, with distinct run IDs and separate runtimes, produce disjoint and correctly attributed correlation maps, including success/failure overlap.

A node failure prevents dependent work and cannot be presented as an ETLantic success or a successful outer flow merely because a failed report was returned; report evidence remains recoverable through the existing runtime contract.
Ready branches obey the resolved concurrency limit; partial selection preserves dependency closure.
Cancellation and timeout are exercised where supported; unqualified requirements receive deterministic support findings rather than positive claims.
Outer Prefect retries remain disabled for effectful ETL execution; ETLantic retry decisions are preserved.
Core import isolation, scheduler discovery, existing report keys, and the `PMADP500` rejection of direct adaptive `/2` remain compatible.

issue_acceptance_map.title: [feature][etlantic-prefect] Define managed execution references and admission ownership

acceptance_criteria.criterion: ADR fixes public reference/factory/targeted-execution interfaces, compatibility/version rules, payload bounds, retention requirements, and diagnostic codes.
Reference decoding rejects unknown schemas, tampering, scope mismatch, and unsupported version combinations before connector I/O.
Runtime construction uses trusted deployment configuration; run parameters cannot select arbitrary import paths, URLs, backend factories, credentials, job variables, or tenant authority.
Direct and managed capability claims are separate; adding managed mode does not remove direct `require_deployment` rejection or imply external DAG compilation.
Initial managed support is an explicitly qualified static-batch `/1` matrix. Adaptive `/2`, streaming, maps, and branches remain rejected until separately qualified.
Duplicate references resolve to the same accepted work; cancelled, expired, revoked, or terminal work cannot start a new effectful attempt by virtue of a Prefect rerun.
Tests exercise authorize-before-lookup, accepted authority, hash/version drift, secret-free payloads, and public installed-artifact imports.

issue_acceptance_map.title: [feature][etlantic-prefect] Add importable managed flows with worker-side runtime reconstruction

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An installed-package subprocess executes an accepted immutable reference with no live submitter objects; the submitter can exit before execution starts.
Targeted execution processes only the referenced submission and never drains unrelated accepted work.
Worker admission verifies pinned plan, code, trust, scope, and resource evidence before any connector effect.
Duplicate concurrent invocations and duplicate delivery cannot create competing authorized effectful owners; losing/terminal invocations have documented no-op/rejection outcomes.
ETLantic report/event/artifact publication preserves accepted run, submission, attempt, fencing, and workspace identities.
Failed, cancelled, timed-out, unknown-effect, and failed-publication outcomes have tested Prefect mappings with no loss of durable evidence.
Lease loss and worker interruption invoke existing recovery rules; uncertain writes require reconciliation and are never blindly replayed.
Worker imports remain FastAPI-free, secrets stay out of Prefect parameters/results/logs, and resources close only after active execution drains.

issue_acceptance_map.title: [feature][etlantic-prefect] Register versioned managed deployments for Prefect work pools

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The adapter registers the importable flow and returns deployment ID, resolved configuration fingerprint, and code/version evidence.
Stable specification/identity supports documented repeat registration and update behavior; conflicting ownership/version changes are surfaced rather than silently retargeted.
Process-pool integration executes in a distinct worker process against the configured server and durable backend.
Worker verifies expected code/environment evidence at admission; mutable branch/tag drift cannot run a different accepted plan unnoticed.
Run parameters and caller job-variable overrides cannot replace trusted entrypoints, backend credentials, images, scopes, or infrastructure policy.
Validate unsupported pool/features and incompatible Prefect versions clearly; import and local direct execution contact no deployment service.
Document explicit update/rollback and drain behavior; replacing a deployment cannot erase accepted-work or effect evidence.

issue_acceptance_map.title: [feature][etlantic-prefect] Dispatch accepted work durably with idempotent Prefect run creation

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Durable acceptance precedes dispatch; a caller's acceptance receipt does not depend on Prefect availability or mean execution succeeded.
Test crashes before creation, after server acceptance but before response, after correlation persistence, and before dispatch acknowledgement.
Retrying ambiguous creation uses the same scoped key, deployment, and parameters and resolves the existing flow run under the qualified Prefect contract.
Multiple dispatchers and duplicate outbox delivery converge on one dispatch record; worker fencing remains authoritative even if extra remote runs exist.
Same dispatch identity with different payload/deployment fingerprint fails with a conflict; deliberate redispatch/retry generations require explicit authorized recovery.
Bounded backoff, queue limits, terminal dispatch diagnostics, orphan reconciliation, and API outage/restart behavior are documented and tested.
Expired/revoked/cancelled work is checked at dispatch and worker admission; tags or keys do not leak sensitive scope information.
No distributed-transaction or exactly-once external-effect claim is made; unknown commit states remain blocked for reconciliation.

issue_acceptance_map.title: [feature][etlantic-prefect] Expose scoped run status, correlation, cancellation, and reconciliation

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Publish a reviewed state/outcome mapping covering queued, running, completed, failed, cancelling, cancelled, crashed, missing remote run, stale observation, failed publication, and reconciliation-required.
Authorization precedes lookup and respects accepted scope and disclosure policy; callers cannot cancel/read another tenant's run by supplying a Prefect ID.
Completed orchestration without successful ETL evidence is not reported as ETL success; Prefect crash/cancellation cannot erase known or uncertain effects.
Test cancellation before dispatch, between dispatch and claim, during staging/publication, after terminal success, and after lost cancellation response.
Repeated cancellation is idempotent; terminal outcomes and effect records are never rewritten merely to match a late Prefect state.
Forced process termination and expired leases recover through canonical ETLantic logic; unknown writes expose reconciliation-required and prohibit automatic rerun.
Status reads are bounded, redacted, and do not execute work, resolve execution secrets, or mutate effect state.
Preserve existing report metadata keys and add verified Prefect correlation without treating synthetic identifiers as observed remote IDs.

issue_acceptance_map.title: [feature][etlantic-prefect] Integrate recurring triggers through canonical schedule admission

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Manual and scheduled paths share canonical admission, revision/policy/resource checks, accepted authority, and durable work.
Duplicate/replayed Prefect triggers for the same schedule revision and nominal time return the same accepted occurrence rather than rerunning effects.
Each new occurrence receives fresh admission and its own execution reference; no recurring execution deployment reuses a fixed accepted reference.
Define and test timezone/DST, cron/interval support, misfire, bounded catch-up, overlap, pause/resume/delete, and revision changes; unsupported parity fails explicitly.
Only the designated timer authority creates occurrences; switching authority handles pending firings and old triggers without duplicate acceptance.
Restart across preparation, firing claim, accept, link, and dispatch recovers using existing ETLantic semantics.
Test revocation, approval expiry, credential changes, schedule amendment, and cancelled occurrences without falling back to newer unapproved definitions.
Prefect-native support is advertised only for the tested semantic matrix; otherwise the ETLantic-timer/Prefect-dispatch path remains the supported path.

issue_acceptance_map.title: [feature][etlantic-prefect] Qualify managed recovery and document FastAPI/Posit Connect composition

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Blocking CI covers direct-mode compatibility plus real installed subprocess and self-hosted Prefect/Process-worker execution; fakes and skips are labelled separately from live proof.
PostgreSQL qualification covers two dispatchers/workers, restart, response loss, duplicate delivery, lease expiry/fencing, and delayed report/event/artifact publication.
Fault tests cover worker death before effects, during an uncertain external write, and after an effect but before durable result publication; no blind replay or invented success.
Credential revocation, cross-scope references, code/plan tampering, unsupported plan schemas/features, quota pressure, cancellation, and infrastructure outages fail with durable, redacted evidence.
Global Prefect persistence/cache/retry defaults cannot leak data or skip/repeat effectful execution outside the adapter policy.
FastAPI composition uses existing canonical services and durable acceptance; tests exercise HTTP/headless parity and API restart without losing accepted work.
Document secrets, retention, reconciliation, deployment update/rollback, graceful drain, least-privilege roles, metrics, and limits; do not claim universal pool support or exactly-once effects.
Posit Connect instructions distinguish a documented recipe from live Connect qualification and include ASGI entrypoint/dependency configuration and external-role reachability.
Update package README, Prefect example, scheduler plan, capability/maturity table, and stale version references as part of implementation; core installation remains Prefect/FastAPI-free.

evidence: The frozen-clock cleanup test denies deletion one second before the configured 30-day cutoff and permits it at the exact cutoff.
The bounded live deployment cleanup uses a test-only zero-age override and verifies route/reference checks, paused binding state, and delete-response recovery.

evidence_scope_exclusions.claim: Independent adopter or external consumer evidence
External identity-provider or third-party provider/connector live evidence
A real-time 30-day retention wait or other elapsed wall-clock evidence
Sustained production capacity, prolonged outage, other simultaneous fault combinations, untested operating systems, Prefect versions, server/client skews, worker pools, plan families, or connectors
